clue.text: Anxiety shown by South American writer beginning to study English

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
US, as in US citizen, stands for American
a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer

indicators.note: the beginning to the word study means only its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An American author feels nervous about starting to study English.
explanation.walkthrough: S and US together make the 'South American', then PEN, then S from 'beginning to study', then E.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious uncertainty while waiting to learn an outcome is what this word names, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Where children play — ultimately yours and mine

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word yours

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A playground spot is described as finally belonging to us both.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of sand set out for young children to dig and build in is a playground feature.

clue.text: Underlying subject — an anomaly

indicators.note: an anomaly is something irregular, so the letters of subject an are put out of order

explanation.surface: A hidden topic turns out to be an oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical word for lying beneath or below something, so lying under.

clue.text: Tragic drama chosen by the Academy

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
RA is the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: The Academy picks a tragedy to stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles and Euripides each wrote a Greek tragedy with this title, about Agamemnon's vengeful daughter.

clue.text: Contrary fates engulfing vicar — at heart philosophical

indicators.note: engulfing means one piece swallows the other inside it
contrary means the word for fates is read the other way round

parts.note: lots are fates, as in one's lot in life

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letters of the word vicar

explanation.surface: Perverse destiny swallows up a clergyman who is philosophical at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' turns the word for fates backwards and 'engulfing' wraps it round the heart of VICAR; 'at heart' means everything but the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting misfortune calmly is the philosophical attitude of the Stoic school, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Changing sides at the start of the match? What a lout!

indicators.text: Changing sides at the start of
indicators.note: sides here are right and left, so the opening right letter is changed for a left one

parts.note: a rubber is a match, as in bridge or a series of games

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a player who switches ends early in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing sides at the start of' swaps the R (right) that opens RUBBER for an L (left). 'What a' is surface padding around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a clumsy, oafish fellow, the same sense as lout; sailors used it for a clumsy landsman.

clue.text: Silver shilling in protective covering

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling

explanation.surface: A silver shilling is wrapped up for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm long-legged underwear worn to protect against cold is covering for the body.

clue.text: Go to pieces although ahead after the interval

indicators.note: after places ahead behind the interval word

parts.note: a break is an interval or pause
up means ahead, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A team collapses despite leading once play restarts.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall apart or disintegrate, both literally and emotionally, is to go to pieces.

clue.text: Declare support for party after course in Irish

indicators.note: in means the course and party sit inside the Irish word

parts.note: Erse is the Irish Gaelic language
a course is a direction, here N for north
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An Irishman backs a party once the meal course is over.
explanation.walkthrough: A course can be a compass heading, so 'course' gives N; 'after' puts the party behind it, and 'in' sets both inside the Irish language.
explanation.definitionFit: To back publicly or give approval to something is to declare support for it.

clue.text: Duchess, perhaps, won OBE and left husband

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Duchess, perhaps, won OBE and left husband' as printed: letters fit WON OBE + L (left) rearranged plus MAN (husband), but no word signals the anagram; 'and' would be doing a job it cannot.
annotationWithheld.clue: Duchess, perhaps, won OBE and left husband

clue.text: Nordic verse written in impassioned dactyls

indicators.note: the letters sit written inside the run of the words impassioned dactyls, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A poet writes northern poetry in fiery dactylic metre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Icelandic collections of Old Norse mythological and heroic poems are known by this name.

clue.text: Useful card for a humorist

parts.note: practical means useful, serving a purpose
the joker is a playing card in a standard pack

explanation.surface: A handy playing card is just the thing for a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster who plays tricks on others is a kind of humorist, if a mischievous one.

clue.text: Wild elation the Pobble could not show

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of elation are running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A nonsense creature is too overjoyed to display its feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pobble is Edward Lear's 'Pobble Who Has No Toes', so he could show no part of a toe; 'Wild' reworks ELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's Pobble lost all his toes, so the nail of one is something he could never display.

clue.text: 11 can be batting and arguing, about bowling at the tail

indicators.note: about means the batting and arguing words go around the bowling letter

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
rowing (rhyming with cowing) means quarrelling

indicators.note: at the tail means the last letter of bowling

explanation.surface: A cricketer batting and quarrelling about the bowling at the end of the order.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across. ROWING here is the British word for arguing, said to rhyme with cowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail on the foot can grow inward into the flesh, so this describes what it can become.

clue.text: Travelling salespersons become rough individuals

parts.note: skin that chaps becomes rough and cracked in cold weather
men are individual people

explanation.surface: Door-to-door sellers turn into coarse people.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for pedlars or hawkers who went from place to place selling goods.

clue.text: Preserve ruin, getting a medal, perhaps

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: perhaps signals that a medal is only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A spoilt jam wins an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam made from citrus fruit is a kind of preserve.

clue.text: Indignation is not in fashion!

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the rage is the current fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: Someone is indignant at being told they are not fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce anger at an injustice is a near synonym for indignation.

clue.text: Open secret — in Paris one gets ahead

indicators.note: gets ahead puts the French word in front of the secret word

parts.note: un is French for one
close means secretive, keeping things to oneself

explanation.surface: A secret everyone knows gets out in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or poetic verb meaning to unfasten, the reverse of shutting, so to open.

clue.text: The bounder said "No thanks" and stayed for the night

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'The bounder said "No thanks" and stayed for the night' as printed: ROO (bounder) is clear, but no parse found for how 'said "No thanks"' gives STED.
annotationWithheld.clue: The bounder said "No thanks" and stayed for the night

clue.text: A graceful vessel returns to the old kingdom

indicators.note: returns tells us the graceful vessel is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: airy means light and graceful in movement
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: An elegant ship sails back to an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses graceful and vessel together as one run, giving SSYRIA to follow the opening A; SS (steamship) is a standard crossword vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Mesopotamian empire centred on the Tigris, a kingdom of the distant past.

clue.text: Each occasion is hitherto unsurpassed

parts.note: all can mean each and every one
a time is an occasion, as in the first time

explanation.surface: Every event is a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A record that has never been beaten before is the best ever, so unsurpassed till now.

clue.text: Created a record although behind in the match

explanation.surface: A team made history even though trailing in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a player losing by a set is a set behind, giving the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing something down creates a record of it; and being a set behind in tennis leaves a player trailing in the match.

clue.text: Replies to serves

explanation.surface: Someone returns tennis serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses are replies; and something that meets a need or does the job serves its purpose.

clue.text: Pretended sadness when throwing out old art deco relics

indicators.note: throwing out suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone fakes grief while clearing out antique Art Deco junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing out' looks like a deletion signal but rearranges O (old) with ART DECO RELICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere weeping, after the legend that the reptile weeps while devouring its prey, means a show of false sorrow.

clue.text: Subject to debate in assembly

explanation.surface: A topic is up for argument at a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A point open to argument is debatable; historically the word also named a local meeting or court of freemen.

clue.text: Ask about attempt by artist to liven up

indicators.note: about means the asking word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to invite someone is to ask them along
a go is an attempt
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is asked to try to brighten things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To energize or refresh is to liven up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Salt water trail

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
to dog someone is to follow or trail them

explanation.surface: A path across brine.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, as is an old sea hand of this name.

clue.text: Small-minded head shows malice

parts.note: mean means petty and small-minded
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Sheerness or Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A petty boss displays spite.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland or promontory, common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitefulness and nastiness are both shades of ill will, so the two words are synonyms.
